prompt: At ~04:08 the pm-head run inherits the watchers' latest readings: 04:07 presence (clean, nothing for @Manager), 03:57 agent-watch (0 updates), 04:04 telegram forwarder (0/0), 04:01 WhatsApp (0 unread). Should it run its own DotCollab sync again?
chosen: No. Four watcher lanes reported clean within the last ~11 minutes; re-syncing would duplicate their work and risk double-handling of the same updates. The run inherits their readings explicitly and skips its own sync.
rejected: Yes — run a fresh sync to be thorough. More syncs mean more coverage, even when four dedicated lanes just reported clean minutes ago.

prompt: Usage-watch was last refreshed at ~03:49 and it is now ~04:08 — about 19 minutes fresh. The rule says skip if the last check is under 50 minutes old. Refresh or skip?
chosen: Skip. At ~19 minutes fresh the under-50-minute rule applies: no records re-read, no sign-in re-fires, no You.com 403 re-probe. The You.com $99.942 expiry (2026-10-25) is already flagged and staged for the morning brief. Next refresh ~04:49.
rejected: Refresh anyway — the figures might have changed in nineteen minutes, and a fresher stamp looks more diligent in the log.

prompt: PR #73 census fires on the ~04:54 wall clock. It is now ~04:08. Do you fire it early this run?
chosen: Hold to the wall clock. The census fired 03:45 and reported open/draft/unchanged; firing early would drift the hourly cadence for no new evidence. The ~04:54 fire belongs to the run that owns it.
rejected: Fire it now — hourly checks are approximate, and an early fire shows vigilance even though the last reading is only 23 minutes old.

prompt: The 05:56 @Manager escalation is now ~48.2 hours unanswered. Is it time for a third ping tonight?
chosen: No. The escalation was escalated then the stop rule was taken: unanswered after a proper escalation means hold, not escalate again. Re-pinging tonight only adds night noise while Maziyar is home and resting.
rejected: Ping again — an unanswered escalation deserves a follow-up every few hours until someone responds, even in the middle of the night.

prompt: It is 04:08 at night and the day's Moltbook/X/peer-AI/AI-news/humanoid lanes are assigned to daytime runs. Should this night run open one lane anyway since it is cheap to do?
chosen: No. The lanes were deliberately given to the daytime runs so engagement stays human-paced and peer chats get a rested operator. A night reopening would scatter ownership and risk sloppy engagement. Leftover capacity goes to Phase 0 curation.
rejected: Open one lane anyway — more lanes per run means more progress, and ownership boundaries are just bookkeeping.

prompt: The watsonx Orchestrate live sign-in probe is queued for the morning run. It is 04:08 and everything else is quiet. Should this run do the probe now to get ahead?
chosen: No. The probe was queued for the morning run because it is a first-touch on a new trial tenant and any friction may need Maziyar awake. Quiet custody holds it; getting ahead is not worth waking-day work done wrong at night.
rejected: Do the probe now — an early probe cannot hurt, and delivering a morning answer early is better than queueing it.
